findings.summary: Continue now accepts the invitation, but it has no invokes link to operation.invite.accept and lacks that operation's preconditions and failure handling: valid unused credential, distinct invitee, no block, and concurrent redemption.
findings.evidence: Continue effects: 'Login continuation from an invitation accepts it for the invitee once sign-in succeeds'; preconditions only '[Not signed in]'; failure only 'Provider unavailable shows the shared ErrorSummary'. operation.invite.accept requires 'Signed-in distinct invitee, Valid unused credential, No block in either direction' and refuses self-connection or block. Only affordance.ConsentPanel.accept invokes operation.invite.accept.

findings.summary: SignInForm now names the inviter, which contradicts the sign-in screen's rule of no private content and its anonymous-only role.
findings.evidence: SignInForm: 'when opened from an invitation it names the inviter'; screen.signin: 'One SignInForm with one Continue control and one privacy link; no private content', roles: [anonymous]

findings.summary: ConsentPanel is now shown only to already-signed-in invitees, which conflicts with the invitation screen and the panel's cardinality, both of which require a ConsentPanel after every validation.
findings.evidence: ConsentPanel description: 'Shown to invitees who open the invitation while already signed in'; cardinality: 'exactly one after validation'; screen.invitation: 'Exactly InvitePreview and ConsentPanel after validation; Accept and Decline controls'
